M-TUI-RECORDS.Name: Records screen and help routing
M-TUI-RECORDS.Purpose: Retain workout sessions, performances, sets, and catalog definitions as domain objects; render a compact records workspace and route a separate full-screen catalog, dialogs, help, setup, and transfers.
M-TUI-RECORDS.Boundary: Ownership includes all listed records helpers. TUI state retains domain models; generic dialog components remain reusable presentation infrastructure.
M-TUI-RECORDS.Behavior: Records show only Sessions <1> in the left fifth and Performances <2> above Sets <3> splitting the remaining four fifths. Pane outer spacing is zero vertical/one horizontal cell, and inner padding is zero vertical/one horizontal cell; the same shared BaseStyle and PanelSpacing apply to catalog, help, setup and dialogs. 1/2/3 focus records panes and Enter advances sessions to performances to sets. n in Performances opens the separate full-screen catalog; there is no catalog column or focus shortcut on records. Session/performance changes filter descendants, records keep their existing border counters, and sets have no date separators. Both the catalog and workout performance tables display Name and Body Weight % from the same catalog definition formatter. The records footer renders only ? - help as a shortcut, using the same outer panel spacing and padding-aware wrapping as tables; real errors and transfer outcomes remain visible. n creates/selects a numbered session immediately and d deletes it; e does nothing in Sessions. The session table contains only Index. n/e/d manage sets; performance d removes only that membership and its sets, and performance e has no independent edit. Help/setup/dialog/catalog input is isolated. Save/load prevent unsafe overlap and preserve IDs on version-4 restore. Mouse input is ignored.

M-TUI-HELP.Name: Records keyboard help
M-TUI-HELP.Purpose: Render titled shortcut groups in responsive columns with aligned descriptions and active-color keys, without an extra page heading.
M-TUI-HELP.Behavior: Navigation documents up/down, gg first row, G last row, and enter select. Actions use n new record, e edit record, d delete record, r reset setup, l load backup, and s save backup. Pages and 1/2/3 focus descriptions are omitted from help; actual keyboard bindings remain unchanged. Wide layouts place Navigation above Actions on the left and Help in the top-right position formerly occupied by Pages. Compact layouts stack Navigation, Actions and Help. Shared spacing is zero vertical/one horizontal with a two-cell column gap and no extra blank rows between groups. Any key returns from help without running its records action; help does not access persistence.

M-TUI-STARTER.Name: Application input wrapper
M-TUI-STARTER.Purpose: Load the records model and intercept Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Z as application-wide quit commands before child input handling.
M-TUI-STARTER.Behavior: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Z emit quit outside help. In help every key, including both control shortcuts, is delegated so it returns to records rather than quitting.

M-TUI-QUESTIONNAIRE.Name: First-start and reset questionnaire
M-TUI-QUESTIONNAIRE.Purpose: Collect optional weight-unit and Dropbox identity answers before opening records, with staged persistence and main-view full-screen styling.
M-TUI-QUESTIONNAIRE.Behavior: Missing preferences trigger optional setup; r reopens it without deleting anything. Stage numeric kg/lb and optional Dropbox answers and save only at completion; Escape restores record state. Authorization, code exchange, and persistence run asynchronously with cancellation, stale-message rejection, retry, and a scrollable authorization URL view. Successful preference changes reformat domain weights for display without mutating cached weights. Use the shared zero vertical/one horizontal inner and outer padding, with single line breaks between content blocks and in the URL disclosure. Keep full-screen framing and native cursors bounded at compact sizes.

M-APP-QUESTIONNAIRE.Name: Questionnaire completion and authorization port
M-APP-QUESTIONNAIRE.Purpose: Define optional authorized-account answers and persist explicit preferences, identity, and credentials atomically.
M-APP-QUESTIONNAIRE.Behavior: Validate models through constructors and matching identity IDs. An empty completion returns before opening a transaction; explicit answers save through one transaction and roll back together on failure. Bootstrap wires real Dropbox linking using the configured key: a nonempty runtime DROPBOX_APP_KEY overrides the release-embedded default. Access and refresh tokens are persisted in the local SQLite database.

M-INFRA-DROPBOX-AUTH.Name: Dropbox authorization
M-INFRA-DROPBOX-AUTH.Purpose: Authorize a real Dropbox account with S256 PKCE and return validated identity and credential models for local persistence.
M-INFRA-DROPBOX-AUTH.Behavior: Open a browser authorization URL with offline access, account_info.read, files.content.read, and files.content.write scopes, and explicit reapproval, omit redirect_uri and client secret, and exchange the pasted authorization code with its verifier. Requests are bounded and cancellation-aware; browser-launch failure exposes the URL and HTTP errors are sanitized. DROPBOX_BROWSER optionally chooses a browser using literal process arguments. The reported Safari consent-page failure remains unconfirmed and is not attributed to its /1 URL prefix. Use the verified token-response account ID. Validate the returned access and refresh tokens through the identity credentials constructor.

M-DOMAIN-IDENTITY.Name: Remote provider identity
M-DOMAIN-IDENTITY.Purpose: Represent Dropbox identity and local access and refresh token credentials with repository ports.
M-DOMAIN-IDENTITY.Behavior: Identity IDs are strings, the provider enum is Dropbox, and credentials contain access and refresh token fields and timestamps. Ports use model-specific IdentityRepository and IdentityCredentialsRepository names in corresponding source files. The credentials port supports deterministic latest-account lookup.

M-DOMAIN-USER-PREFERENCES.Name: User preferences
M-DOMAIN-USER-PREFERENCES.Purpose: Represent persisted weight unit selection through its repository.
M-DOMAIN-USER-PREFERENCES.Behavior: Preference updates use the application transaction runner and keep weight unit selection persisted. Reads return an existence flag and a validated in-memory kg default without creating a row; only explicit saves create preferences.

M-APP-REMOTE-STATE.Name: Validated workout backup application
M-APP-REMOTE-STATE.Purpose: Validate versioned workout snapshots and orchestrate local export, Dropbox save, and atomic local restore.
M-APP-REMOTE-STATE.Behavior: Application ports exchange version-4 snapshots containing catalog exercises, workout sessions, performances, sets, and preferences. Save exports one consistent snapshot. Load validates all references and duplicate membership before atomic replacement. Old backups are rejected and local credentials remain intact.

M-DOMAIN-STATE.Name: Workout state snapshot
M-DOMAIN-STATE.Purpose: Represent versioned workout snapshots and validate cross-model invariants independently of storage or transfer mechanisms.
M-DOMAIN-STATE.Behavior: Only snapshot version 4 is accepted. Snapshots contain catalog exercises, whole-workout sessions, performances, sets, and optional preferences. Constructor validation rejects duplicate IDs, duplicate catalog names, duplicate membership pairs, invalid positive unique session indices/timestamps, missing session/catalog parents, and orphaned sets. Empty workouts and performances are preserved. Old versions fail before local writes. Credentials and identities remain excluded; SQLite storage bounds are enforced by persistence.

M-INFRA-DROPBOX-STATE.Name: Dropbox workout snapshot adapter
M-INFRA-DROPBOX-STATE.Purpose: Upload and download /trainings-logger/data.json with local credentials, public-client token refresh, and bounded payloads.
M-INFRA-DROPBOX-STATE.Behavior: Select the latest credential update deterministically, verify the Dropbox account, and use its local access and refresh tokens. Refresh expired access tokens using the app key and refresh token, saving replacement credentials before transfer; retry one provider-reported expired-token response. Upload overwrites the fixed backup path and sends application/octet-stream; download sends no Content-Type or request body and strictly decodes and validates a snapshot with a 16 MiB limit. Bounded HTTP requests report missing accounts/backups, permissions, and network errors without exposing response bodies or credentials. Required-scope HTTP 400/401 failures tolerate provider app-ID wording and single/double quoted scope names. JSON missing_scope tags and documented legacy endpoint-authorization failures also name the required file permission with App Console submission and relinking instructions. Unclassified HTTP 400 failures retain only a bounded hexadecimal Dropbox request ID. Version-4 payloads include workouts, performances, and performance-owned sets; old payloads fail validation before import.

M-INFRA-PERSISTENCE-SQLITE.Name: SQLite workout and identity persistence
M-INFRA-PERSISTENCE-SQLITE.Purpose: Persist catalog definitions, whole-workout sessions, performances, sets, preferences, and local identities/credentials; export and atomically restore version-4 workout snapshots.
M-INFRA-PERSISTENCE-SQLITE.Behavior: A single CLI-generated initial migration creates seven application tables for fresh databases. Sessions contain UUID id, positive unique integer index, and created_at. Creation queries the maximum existing index inside its transaction and adds one, starting at 1; listing sorts by descending index. Deletion leaves remaining indices unchanged. performances reference a session and catalog exercise, enforce unique(session_id, exercise_id), and list in created_at ASC/id ASC insertion order. Session deletion cascades memberships and sets; catalog deletion is restricted while referenced. Repeated adds are idempotent through unique-pair insertion and lookup. Sets reference performance_id and order newest first. SQL defaults use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; edits retain ownership and timestamps. Down drops tables in dependency-safe order; up/down/up recreates the baseline. Version-4 export preserves empty workouts/performances. Import validates first and replaces workout tables atomically with membership deletion/insertion in foreign-key order, retaining credentials and rolling back on failures. Existing databases using earlier baselines need separate handling; the application does not reset them.

M-DOMAIN-EXERCISE.Name: Exercise domain model
M-DOMAIN-EXERCISE.Purpose: Construct validated exercises with non-empty identifiers, names, and bounded body-weight shares.
M-DOMAIN-EXERCISE.Behavior: NewExercise validates reusable catalog definitions with nonempty IDs/names and bounded body-weight shares; persistence reads reconstruct models through the constructor. Definitions can be referenced by performances in many workouts. Deletion of a referenced definition is rejected to preserve history.

M-DOMAIN-SET.Name: Workout set domain model
M-DOMAIN-SET.Purpose: Construct validated sets owned by performances and validated exercise weights.
M-DOMAIN-SET.Behavior: NewSet requires set and PerformanceID values and validates weight and rest. JSON uses performance_id. Creation timestamps remain for deterministic ordering; edits retain original ownership and timestamps. Persistence reads reconstruct through constructors.

M-DOMAIN-SHARED-WEIGHT.Name: Shared weight values and units
M-DOMAIN-SHARED-WEIGHT.Purpose: Represent validated weights and weight-unit enum values.
M-DOMAIN-SHARED-WEIGHT.Behavior: NewWeight and NewWeightUnit validate values; unit enums remain in their own source file.

M-DOMAIN-SESSION.Name: Workout sessions
M-DOMAIN-SESSION.Purpose: Represent whole workouts with validated UUID identity, positive integer index, and UTC creation time, independent of catalog exercise definitions.
M-DOMAIN-SESSION.Behavior: NewSession validates UUID identity, a positive integer index, and supported creation time, defaulting to UTC now when omitted. Sessions have neither Title nor ExerciseID. Empty workouts are allowed. Repository ports save, find, compute maximum index plus one, list by descending index, and delete workouts. Indices remain stable when other workouts are deleted.

M-APP-SESSIONS.Name: Workout session operations
M-APP-SESSIONS.Purpose: Create, delete, and list automatically numbered whole-workout sessions without requiring a catalog exercise.
M-APP-SESSIONS.Behavior: Create has no input fields, queries the maximum existing index plus one and generates a UUID in its transaction. List returns workouts by descending index. No rename operation exists. Delete cascades memberships and sets through persistence. Empty sessions remain valid. Each use case has one operation per file and a transaction runner.

M-DOMAIN-PERFORMANCE.Name: Workout performances
M-DOMAIN-PERFORMANCE.Purpose: Represent one reusable exercise added to one workout session.
M-DOMAIN-PERFORMANCE.Behavior: NewPerformance validates UUID identity, required session/catalog IDs, and UTC insertion time. Repository ports save once per pair, find by ID or pair, list by workout, and delete performances. The model stores no duplicate catalog name or set data.

M-APP-PERFORMANCES.Name: Workout performances and sets
M-APP-PERFORMANCES.Purpose: Add, list, and remove workout performances and operate on their sets.
M-APP-PERFORMANCES.Behavior: AddPerformance validates both parents and returns the unique existing or created performance in one transaction. ListPerformances preserves insertion order. DeletePerformance affects only that workout performance and its sets. Set creation/listing use PerformanceID; creation rejects missing performances and edits retain their original owner and timestamp.

M-TUI-CATALOG.Name: Full-screen exercise catalog
M-TUI-CATALOG.Purpose: Select and manage reusable exercise definitions in an isolated full-screen view.
M-TUI-CATALOG.Boundary: Own catalog input, entry/return behavior, and full-screen table/error rendering. RecordsModel retains shared catalog data/table state; editing and membership operations delegate to the existing records actions and application handlers.
M-TUI-CATALOG.Behavior: n in workout Performances opens catalog, retains records error and selection, clears pending g, and refreshes domain data. Enter adds/selects the highlighted definition and returns to Performances; duplicates select the existing membership. Esc returns without adding a performance and restores records errors and browsing state. Catalog n/e/d manage definitions, forms save/cancel back into catalog, and referenced deletion remains protected. Local errors stay in catalog. Records focus/save/load/setup/help/quit shortcuts cannot trigger records actions here. Keyboard row/page/half-page/gg/G navigation remains available, and mouse input is ignored. Catalog and forms resize within terminal bounds. The table shows Name and Body Weight % using the shared formatter. No shortcut/help footer is rendered; the table uses all available height when there is no error, and actual local errors appear with the same outer spacing as tables.

M-TUI-COMPONENTS.Name: Shared TUI spacing and modal geometry
M-TUI-COMPONENTS.Purpose: Keep every view on the same compact padding and render bounded modal forms with matching native cursors.
M-TUI-COMPONENTS.Behavior: BaseStyle and PanelSpacing use zero vertical/one horizontal padding. Records/catalog, help and setup share those styles. Dialogs retain centered overlays with shared inner padding, consecutive wide field rows, compact label/input rows, and no extra blank help rows. Field sizing and native cursor offsets derive from the shared frame; tiny forms and cursors stay bounded.

M-CLI-BUILD-CONFIG.Name: CLI build configuration
M-CLI-BUILD-CONFIG.Purpose: Resolve the public Dropbox app key from a runtime override or build-time default.
M-CLI-BUILD-CONFIG.Behavior: A package-main string dropboxAppKey is settable with Go -X linker flags. configuredDropboxAppKey returns a trimmed nonempty runtime DROPBOX_APP_KEY first, otherwise the embedded default. Unconfigured source builds keep an empty default and optional Dropbox setup. No user credentials or app secret are embedded.

M-RELEASE.Name: Tagged CLI releases
M-RELEASE.Purpose: Build and publish CLI release artifacts with the public Dropbox app key supplied at build time.
M-RELEASE.Behavior: On v* tags, GitHub Actions checks out the repository, selects Go from go.mod, exposes vars.DROPBOX_APP_KEY as a job environment variable, and rejects a missing key before running GoReleaser. GoReleaser injects it using -X main.dropboxAppKey and builds linux/darwin/windows for amd64/arm64. Existing GITHUB_TOKEN and contents:write permissions publish release artifacts. The repository variable is public configuration; no access/refresh tokens or app secret are embedded.
